column1: Using the Beige Book as context, the FOMC statement’s characterization holds: activity grew at a modest-to-moderate pace across districts, with consumer spending steady to slightly firmer and tourism stronger in parts of the Southeast. Labor markets remained tight nationwide, with notable shortages of lower‑skill workers, ongoing wage pressures reported by districts and staffing agencies, and firms enhancing benefits to attract workers—consistent with a strong labor market and low unemployment. At the same time, business fixed investment and manufacturing were mixed, residential real estate and construction contributed only modestly, and loan demand was not broadly strong, aligning with softer investment signals and muted inflation. Combining this with the April SLOOS evidence of tighter standards and weaker demand in several loan categories reinforces a cautious, risk‑management stance. Netting these, the Beige Book tempers the SLOOS‑driven dovish tilt slightly (given persistent labor tightness and wage pressures), but the overall tone remains modestly dovish relative to neutral. sentiment score = 0.15
